reviews.review: Absolute piece of crap. First Remnant was a good game. This... This is pathetic in every possible way.
it's definitely not the first game, but it's pretty good so far. i've heard tell of so many secrets and hidden classes, so that's kinda hype to discover.

I’ll post the same review under both Remnant: From the Ashes and Remnant II, since I played and compared them side by side.

I definitely recommend both games—they’re very good—but each has some major strengths and weaknesses. So far, I’ve only finished them on normal difficulty.

Remnant: From the Ashes was much more fun overall. Progressing through the maps felt challenging—you really had to fight your way through. Each boss had a specific pattern you needed to figure out to gain an advantage, which made the fights engaging, although some bosses were nearly impossible and I only beat them thanks to a bug. One downside was that the dodge roll felt pretty clunky. On the other hand, the weapon variety was excellent compared to Remnant II. The maps, however, were visually quite monotonous and exploring them didn’t feel very rewarding. The game also felt a bit short—I wouldn’t have minded if it were twice as long. Overall though, I remember it very positively.

Remnant II was less fun for me. Most of the time I went through the maps like a hot knife through butter, with the exception of N’Erud. Bosses didn’t really have clear patterns—it often felt like mindless shooting until they died. The visuals were more interesting, but still not impressive compared to other games. The maps didn’t feel small as much as they felt chaotic. Even though there are more hidden areas to discover, finding them doesn’t feel rewarding—you end up with tons of rings, but I only found one long gun during my entire playthrough (I know I missed one or two, but even three would still feel lacking).

A big improvement over the first game is the class system—you can choose from multiple classes and even combine two at once, which was a lot of fun. On the other hand, traits were much worse than in the first game: fewer, less interesting, and less satisfying to upgrade. Despite the limited gear, I still ended up extremely overpowered. Some class designs also feel odd—for example, one is built around long-range combat, but you almost never actually fight at that distance, making it pretty pointless.

Remnant II also felt quite short, although maybe that’s just my impression. Other players say it has amazing replayability, so I might change my opinion later.

Anyway, I enjoyed both games. And I'm just hoping the series continues, even though the story doesn’t leave much room for it. Maybe a sequel?
